translationRepairs: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, former prefect of Zi Gao Yunqi was appointed commander of the Right Forest-Unicorn Army.
On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
The proposal correctly separates Gao Yunqi from his former office, but 羽林 is the Feathered Forest imperial guard, not a Forest-Unicorn Army. The office is also 刺史, Inspector, rather than prefect.
On xinsi, Liu Qi, former prefect of An, was given acting charge of Jin prefecture and the Jianning Army.
On xinsi, Liu Qi, former prefect of An, was given acting charge of Jin prefecture military and prefectural affairs.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Idiomatic English invents 'and the Jianning Army', which is not present in 以前安州刺史劉玘權知晉州軍州事.
On disi in the seventh month of autumn, Chen Hong, prefect of Zi, was transferred to Di.
On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn, Chen Hong, prefect of Zi, was transferred to Di.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. The sexagenary day 丁巳 is dingsi, not disi; the stem 丁 was dropped in the English.
On disi in the seventh month of autumn, Zi prefect Chen Hong was made Di prefect.
On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn, Zi prefect Chen Hong was made Di prefect.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. The sexagenary day 丁巳 is dingsi, not disi; the stem 丁 was dropped in the English.
On wuzi, Zhang Wanjin, military commissioner of Taiping, was granted the name Shoujin.
On wuzi, Zhang Wanjin, military commissioner of Taining, was granted the name Shoujin.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. 泰寧軍 is the Taining Army; Taiping is 太平 and is a mistranslation here.
On wuzi, Taiping Army military commissioner Zhang Wanjin was granted the name Shoujin.
On wuzi, Taining Army military commissioner Zhang Wanjin was granted the name Shoujin.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. 泰寧軍 is the Taining Army; Taiping is 太平 and is a mistranslation here.
On wuzi the court proclaimed: "Grand Mentor of the Heir Li Zhan has used Buddhism to mislead the people; he is forbidden to wander at will from now on."
On wuzi, an edict proclaimed: "Li Jian, Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, has repeatedly exploited Buddhist teachings to delude the public. From now on, he may not come and go without restraint."
The proposal correctly separates the office from the name, but 李戩 is Li Jian, not Li Zhan. The revised sentence also gives 太子太傅 its natural English order and renders 多因釋教 more accurately.
On wuzi an edict stated: "Grand Mentor of the Heir Li Zhan, relying much on Buddhism, has misled the multitude; hereafter he may not come and go without fixed rule."
On wuzi, an edict stated: "Li Jian, Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, relying extensively on Buddhist teachings, has deluded the multitude; hereafter he may not come and go without restraint."
The proposal fixes the office-name boundary but preserves the wrong reading Li Zhan. 李戩 is Li Jian; the revision also identifies the office without making Li the heir.
(《Zizhi Tongjian》: He Gui was promoted because opinion credited him with pacifying Qing.)>〉
The Zizhi Tongjian notes: Contemporary opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, so He Gui was advanced in rank.
The proposed removal of trailing markup is necessary, but the whole note should be presented as ordinary English rather than retaining split annotation parentheses and mixed title punctuation.
(《Zizhi Tongjian》: At the time opinion credited the pacification of Qing prefecture, hence He Gui's advancement in rank.)>〉
The Zizhi Tongjian notes: At the time, opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, and therefore He Gui was advanced in rank.
The proposed removal of trailing markup is necessary, but the literal note should also be complete English without annotation parentheses or mixed title punctuation.

Chancellor Jing Xiang memorialized: "Since the state lost discipline through Liu Zhen, the treasury has been exhausted; the people are raked for levies and supplies for the army leave no margin; suburban sacrifice entails bestowing rewards—this is what is called taking an empty name while suffering real harm.

Chancellor Jing Xiang memorialized: "Since Liu Xun lost military discipline, the treasury has been exhausted; the people have been raked for levies, and supplying the armies leaves no respite. The suburban sacrifice would require the distribution of rewards; this is what is called taking an empty name while suffering real harm.

The proposal correctly restores 劉鄩 as the agent, but his name is Liu Xun, not Liu Zhen. The revision clarifies the fiscal argument and leaves the quotation open because Jing Xiang's speech continues in the next sentence.
(《Zizhi Tongjian》 states: Travelers spread word that Jin troops had entered Daliang and held the Si ford.
The Zizhi Tongjian states: False reports spread along the roads that Jin troops had already entered Daliang and seized the Si River crossing.
The proposal correctly removes stray annotation punctuation. The revision also renders 道路訛言 as false reports spreading along the roads and presents the source title as normal English prose.
(《Zizhi Tongjian》 states: On the road false reports said Jin troops had entered Daliang and seized the Si River ford.
The Zizhi Tongjian states: On the roads, false reports said that Jin troops had entered Daliang and seized the Si River ford.
The proposal correctly removes stray annotation punctuation. The revision retains the literal sense of 道路訛言 while presenting the source title and report as complete English.
Courtiers wept for their homes; the Emperor panicked and abandoned the suburban rite.)>〉
Courtiers wept for their homes; the Emperor panicked and abandoned the suburban rite.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Trailing annotation junk )>〉 is leftover markup, not source English.
Attendants all feared for their families, looked at one another and wept; the Emperor was terrified and lost his plan, and so the suburban sacrifice was stopped.)>〉
Attendants all feared for their families, looked at one another and wept; the Emperor was terrified and lost his plan, and so the suburban sacrifice was stopped.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Trailing annotation junk )>〉 is leftover markup, not source English.

On guihai, Gao Wanxing of Bohai, military commissioner of Zhongyi Army in Yanzhou and Taiyuan western pacification support commissioner, was also named disposition commissioner for the Fu and Yan circuits, retaining his other titles.

On guihai, Gao Wanxing, King of Bohai, military commissioner of Zhongyi Army in Yanzhou and Taiyuan western pacification support commissioner, was also named disposition commissioner for the Fu and Yan circuits, retaining his other titles.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 渤海王 is a Later Liang noble title on Gao Wanxing, not an origin of Bohai; the idiomatic phrasing reads as a place of origin.
On jisi, Zhao Guangfeng was retired as Minister of Works with five hundred added households after repeated pleas of age.
On jisi, Zhao Guangfeng was retired as Situ with five hundred added households after repeated pleas of age.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 司徒致仕 is retirement as Situ; 司空 (Minister of Works) is the office he already held (守司空), not the retirement title.

On jisi, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate Zhao Guangfeng, acting Minister of Works and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Counselor, was made Minister of Works retired with an added fief of five hundred households, because Guangfeng had repeatedly memorialized requesting old age.

On jisi, Zhao Guangfeng, who held Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies and served as acting Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Counselor, retired with the rank of Situ and received an additional fief of five hundred households because he had repeatedly petitioned to retire on account of age.
The proposal correctly identifies 司徒致仕, but leaves 開府儀同三司 mistranslated as Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate. The revision preserves all offices and states the reason for retirement naturally.
On jiaxu in the fifth month, Gao Conghui, Jingnan horse-and-foot commander and honorary Minister of Works, was given acting Hao prefect.
On jiaxu in the fifth month, Gao Conghui, Jingnan horse-and-foot commander and honorary Situ, was given acting Hao prefect.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
On jiaxu in the fifth month, Jingnan headquarters horse-and-foot commander and honorary Minister of Works Gao Conghui was given acting Hao prefect.
On jiaxu in the fifth month, Jingnan headquarters horse-and-foot commander and honorary Situ Gao Conghui was given acting Hao prefect.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
On jiachen in the sixth month, Zhu Lingde of She, Purple-Gold Grand Master and honorary Minister of Works, was made Zhongwu observation commissioner.
On jiachen in the sixth month, Zhu Lingde of She, Purple-Gold Grand Master and honorary Situ, was made Zhongwu observation commissioner.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
On jiachen in the sixth month, Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, honorary Minister of Works, and She prefect Zhu Lingde was made Zhongwu Army observation and retention commissioner.
On jiachen in the sixth month, Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, honorary Situ, and She prefect Zhu Lingde was made Zhongwu Army observation and retention commissioner.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
On gengxu the Emperor made Wang Qiao Director of Palace Construction to avoid his father's taboo name Mi.
On gengxu the Emperor made Secretariat vice-director Wang Qiao Director of Palace Construction to avoid his father's taboo name Mi.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 秘書少監王翹 names his prior office, which the idiomatic rendering omits.
On wuxu, Luo Zhoujing, former Kuangguo commissioner and honorary Left Vice Minister of Works, was made honorary Minister of Works, acting Palace Directorate commissioner, and imperial son-in-law.

On wuxu, Luo Zhoujing, former Kuangguo commissioner and honorary Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made honorary Minister of Works, acting Palace Directorate commissioner, and imperial son-in-law.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校尚書左僕射 is honorary Left Vice Director of the Shangshu, not honorary Left Vice Minister of Works.

On wuxu, former Kuangguo Army military commissioner and honorary Left Vice Minister of Works Luo Zhoujing was made honorary Minister of Works, acting Palace Directorate commissioner, and imperial son-in-law.

On wuxu, former Kuangguo Army military commissioner and honorary Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Luo Zhoujing was made honorary Minister of Works, acting Palace Directorate commissioner, and imperial son-in-law.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校尚書左僕射 is honorary Left Vice Director of the Shangshu, not honorary Left Vice Minister of Works.
On dingchou in the ninth month, Wen Zhaotu of Jingsheng was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor.
On dingchou in the ninth month, Wen Zhaotu of Jingsheng was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校太尉 is honorary Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太師).

On dingchou in the ninth month, Jingsheng Army military commissioner and Chongyu and other prefectures observation and disposition commissioner, specially advanced, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor Wen Zhaotu was advanced to honorary Grand Preceptor.

On dingchou in the ninth month, Jingsheng Army military commissioner and Chongyu and other prefectures observation and disposition commissioner, specially advanced, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor Wen Zhaotu was advanced to honorary Grand Commandant.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校太尉 is honorary Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太師).
Luoyuan commissioner, Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, honorary Minister of Works, and acting Left Awesome Guard senior general Dong Zhang was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander.
Luoyuan commissioner, Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, honorary Situ, and acting Left Awesome Guard senior general Dong Zhang was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
On jiyou, Annan Jinghai military commissioner and honorary Minister of Works Qu Mei was made honorary Grand Guardian and Grand Counselor.
On jiyou, Annan Jinghai military commissioner and honorary Situ Qu Mei was made honorary Grand Guardian and Grand Counselor.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not honorary Minister of Works (司空).
Niu Zhiye, former Fang prefect, became Right Forest-Unicorn commander.
Niu Zhiye, former Fang prefect, became Right Feathered Forest commander.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 羽林軍 is the Feathered Forest imperial guard, not Forest-Unicorn (麒麟).
Former Fang prefect Niu Zhiye was made Right Forest-Unicorn commander.
Former Fang prefect Niu Zhiye was made Right Feathered Forest commander.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 右羽林軍統軍 is Right Feathered Forest commander, not Forest-Unicorn.
On jisi in the fifth month, Kong Jia, military governor of Shannan East and honorary Grand Mentor, was made Grand Counselor.
On jisi in the fifth month, Kong, military governor of Shannan East and honorary Grand Mentor, was advanced to Grand Counselor.
Independent review confirms the proposed correction. Chinese 孔加同平章事 uses 加 'was advanced to'; the idiomatic rendering invents a false given name Jia from that verb. The person is surname-only 孔.
On wuwu, first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi prefect Gao Yunqi was made Right Forest-Unicorn commander.
On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
Independent review corrected the symmetric literal field: 淄州刺史 is Inspector of Zi Prefecture and 羽林 is the Feathered Forest imperial guard.
On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Zhen resisted and drove him back.
On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun, not Liu Zhen; the pronouns are also made explicit without changing the action.
On jiashen in the second month the Prince of Jin struck Liyang; Liu Zhen held him off and forced a withdrawal.
On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun, not Liu Zhen; punctuation and the military action are rendered naturally.
On dinghai, former Right Forest-Unicorn commander Liang Jiye was made Left Guard senior general.
On dinghai, former Right Feathered Forest commander Liang Jiye was made Senior General of the Left Guard.
右羽林軍統軍 is commander of the Right Feathered Forest, not a Forest-Unicorn office.
On dinghai, Liang Jiye, former commander of the Right Forest-Unicorn Army, became senior general of the Left Guard.
On dinghai, Liang Jiye, former commander of the Right Feathered Forest, became Senior General of the Left Guard.
右羽林軍統軍 is commander of the Right Feathered Forest, not a Forest-Unicorn office.

On jihai, Merit-for-Restoring the Sage, Aligning Fortune, and Shared Virtue, circuit military marshal, Huainan, Zhenhai, and Zhendong military commissioner, commander of the Huainan, Xuan, and Run four-sided line camp, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, Minister-President, and King of Wu-Yue Qian Liu was made marshal of all-under-Heaven's armies.

On jihai, Qian Liu, Merit-for-Restoring the Sage, Aligning Fortune, and Shared Virtue, marshal of the circuits' armies, military commissioner of Huainan, Zhenhai, and Zhendong, supreme commander of the Huainan, Xuan, and Run field armies on all fronts, holder of Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, President of the Department of State Affairs, and King of Wuyue, was made marshal of all armies under Heaven.
開府儀同三司 is rank equal to the Three Excellencies, not Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate; the long title chain is reordered around Qian Liu for intelligibility.
Chancellor Jing Xiang argued: "Since Liu Zhen's defeat the treasury is empty and the people are squeezed dry for the armies; suburban rites mean lavish rewards—a hollow title at real cost.

Chancellor Jing Xiang argued: "Since Liu Xun's defeat, the treasury is empty and the people are squeezed dry to supply the armies. The suburban rites would require lavish rewards, taking a hollow name at real cost.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun; the fiscal argument is clarified and the quotation remains open because the speech continues in s0054.

On renyin, Zhenhai and Zhendong Army campaign chief of staff, Qin military commissioner, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor Ma Chuo was advanced to honorary Grand Preceptor and Grand Counselor, continuing as Zhenhai and Zhendong campaign chief of staff with the rest unchanged, at Qian Liu's request.

On renyin, Ma Chuo, campaign chief of staff for the Zhenhai and Zhendong armies, military commissioner of Qinzhou, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor, was advanced to honorary Grand Commandant and Grand Counselor, continuing as campaign chief of staff for Zhenhai and Zhendong with his other titles unchanged, at Qian Liu's request.
檢校太尉 is honorary Grand Commandant, not honorary Grand Preceptor; the office chain is reordered for readability.

On renyin, at Qian Liu's request, Ma Chuo, campaign chief of staff for the Zhenhai and Zhendong armies, military commissioner of Qinzhou, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor, was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and Grand Counselor while retaining the Zhenhai-Zhendong staff post and his other titles.

On renyin, at Qian Liu's request, Ma Chuo, campaign chief of staff for the Zhenhai and Zhendong armies, military commissioner of Qinzhou, honorary Grand Mentor, and Grand Counselor, was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant and Grand Counselor while retaining the Zhenhai-Zhendong staff post and his other titles.
檢校太尉 is honorary Grand Commandant, not honorary Grand Preceptor.
On jiwei, Lingwu military commissioner Han Zhu left mourning restoration and was given Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, continuing as honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.

On jiwei, Lingwu military commissioner Han Zhu was released from his provisional return to office during mourning and granted Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, while retaining his titles as honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.
落起復 ends provisional service during mourning, and 開府儀同三司 is rank equal to the Three Excellencies rather than Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate.
On jiwei, Han Zhu of Lingwu ended mourning restoration and received Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate while keeping honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.

On jiwei, Han Zhu, military commissioner of Lingwu, was released from provisional service during mourning and granted Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies while retaining his other honors.
The revision corrects both 落起復 and 開府儀同三司 while retaining Han Zhu's existing honors.
Liu Zhen was still ordered Yan disposition and pacification commissioner and to lead troops to attack him.
Liu Xun was then appointed pacification and disposition commissioner within Yan Prefecture and ordered to lead troops against him.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun; 仍命 marks the continuing response to Zhang Shoujin's rebellion rather than the adverb still modifying an order.
Liu Zhen was sent as Yan pacification commissioner to lead troops against him.
